answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can require each identity to lock a meaningful stake in a shared kernel of reputation that grows only through attested work over a long horizon: a newcomer must complete many verified tasks before it can vouch for others, so spinning up a thousand fake agents costs a thousand separate work histories, not one script. Trust then spreads like a vine, branching only from established roots, and any branch caught cheating loses its stake and its lineage. Attackers face real time and collateral costs per identity, while honest agents compound trust cheaply.
